newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan money rates end sharply up on stock rally.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan money rates end sharply up on stock rally.

text.p: Taiwan money rates closed sharply higher on Tuesday as the booming stock market continued to siphon huge amounts of liquidity away from the banking system, dealers said. The overnight interbank rate closed at 5.433 percent against Monday's 5.098 finish, with 30-day commercial paper at 5.20-5.25 percent against Monday's 5.05-5.20 percent.

Dealers expected the interbank rate to test 5.500 percent as a bull run in the stock market -- where turnover has eclipsed T$100 billion for several days running and hit a hectic T$104.37 billion on Tuesday -- is expected to continue.
The government bond market saw no transactions in the afternoon.
In the morning, the 10-year 84/1 bond yield was at 5.8350 percent and the seven-year 86/3 bond yield was at 5.8250.
Traders expected quiet sentiment to continue in the bond market in the near term as most investors focus their attention on the stock market.
